keyResults.statement: A quantum generalisation of the five-term (pentagon) dilogarithm identity, whose classical limit gives the classical identity; a finite-dimensional realisation on the Fermat curve is also constructed.
keyResults.useForFolio: Source of the pentagon relation carried as a §3b-cond input by the pentagon-ascension conjecture.

relevance.rationale: Identity confirmed from the document's own cover (arXiv:hep-th/9310070v1, dated September/October 1993, quantum dilogarithm, two authors) and matches the seeded key's title and its recorded journal volume/pages. NOTE the duplicate join in this slice: library/arxiv-1002.0126v1/1002.0126v1.pdf was ALSO seeded to faddeev_kashaev1994 and is a different document entirely; this file is the correct one. Seven citation sites, load-bearing, and the substance matches the document's own abstract, which states that a quantum generalisation of Rogers' five-term (pentagon) dilogarithm identity is proposed, that the classical limit gives Rogers' identity, and that in the finite-dimensional realisation the quantum dilogarithm is constructed as a function on the Fermat curve. That is exactly what the pentagon/associator sites use: braids-and-knots/pentagon-uv-commutation-woronowicz.lean:44,297; QuantumObservableUniverses/DilogPentagonAssociator.lean:53; QBeta/CyclicDilogPentagon.lean:52. The remaining sites (LiftingDescent/tm_dilogarithm_evaluation.lean:71,84; QBeta/MonodromyDatumRigidity.lean:54) cite it for the quantum dilogarithm generally. One metadata nit, not a substantive defect: tm_dilogarithm_evaluation.lean:71,84 attach DOI 10.1142/S0217732394002446 while the ref() entry gives 10.1142/S0217732394000447 — the two Ref lines and the entry disagree on the digits.

keyResults.statement: A quantum generalisation of Rogers' five-term pentagon dilogarithm identity, whose classical limit recovers Rogers' identity; in the finite-dimensional case the quantum dilogarithm is realised as a function on the Fermat curve and the identity holds there.
keyResults.useForFolio: It is the primary source for the pentagon identity that the associator, cyclic-pentagon and UV-commutation Lean files cite — and it is the source the ~19 [faddeev1994] sites in this slice arguably should be pointing at for the pentagon specifically, since the document filed under that other key states the pentagon only in passing.
